top_story: Trump’s threat on 23 March to destroy Iran’s power grid unless Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz pushed Tehran toward explicit warnings of regional escalation, sharpening the risk that pressure on a strategic chokepoint could spill into a wider confrontation across the Gulf. That escalation sits within a longer regional pattern in which US and Israeli coercive power is used to preserve dominance over the Gulf’s energy and security order, reinforcing perceptions in Iran and across the region that military pressure is structural rather than episodic. In Israel, the decision to return reservists accused of raping and torturing a Palestinian detainee at Sde Teiman to service signals institutional impunity inside the war apparatus, deepening Palestinian vulnerability and further eroding the credibility of legal restraint. The combined effect is a regional environment in which coercion is normalized from the Gulf to detention sites, raising the likelihood that strategic brinkmanship and human abuse will continue to feed each other.
